title: Resource Levelling
summary: The routine for resource levelling: clashes, options and quick sums, worked at Level 1 and Level 2, with Level 3 knock-ons and exam technique. Quick-sum practice and an exit ticket.

els.text: Finding the minimum time when workers are limited
Level a resource histogram using quick sums to find the minimum completion time.

•  Spot a clash on a resource histogram
•  Work out the quick sum for an option
•  Use the routine to level a histogram (Levels 1 and 2)
•  See what changes at Level 3: a try that leaves another clash
A time when the activities running need more workers than the limit.
Hold back one activity in the clash until the next activity in the clash finishes.
A quick calculation of the earliest an option can possibly let the project finish.
Checking one option properly: hold the activity back and follow what it knocks on.
Another activity that has to start later because something before it now finishes later.

slides.title: The activities

els.text: Each activity needs one worker. Only 2 workers are available. The project takes 23 days with no limit.

slides.brief: Level 1 worked example: eight activities, one worker each, two workers available. The earliest and latest times are already known from earlier lessons.

slides.title: The earliest start histogram

els.text: Every activity starts as early as it can.
Between 12 and 16, E, F and G are all running: 3 workers, but only 2 are available.

slides.brief: Level 1 worked example. Click: the clash, then the reading of it.

els.text: A clash is a time when the activities running need more workers than the limit.

slides.title: Option

els.text: An option is to hold back one activity in the clash until the next activity in the clash finishes.

slides.brief: Show the three options for the clash: E, F, G. For each, name when it is held until.

slides.title: Quick sum

els.text:
New finish: when the activity would finish if it is held back.
LFT: the latest finish time of the activity.
If it still finishes by its LFT, the project time does not change.

slides.brief: The one idea of the lesson. Hold the formula on the board. Unlimited time is the project time with no worker limit.

slides.title: Quick sums at the first clash

els.text: Quick sums at the first clash
Unlimited time = 23 days. The clash is 12 to 16, so the options are E, F and G.
G is held until F finishes at 16, so it finishes at 16 + 8 = 24. Its LFT is 23, so it is 1 day late.

slides.brief: Level 1 worked example. Pupils fill the last three columns, then show the answers. Unlimited time is 23.

slides.title: Why smallest first

els.text: A quick sum is a floor: if you hold this activity back, the project cannot finish any sooner.
So if the smallest quick sum gives a schedule with no clash left, nothing can beat it.
G has the smallest quick sum (24). Try it first.

slides.brief: The reason the routine works. Click through.

slides.title: The routine

els.text: Draw the histogram: every activity as early as it can start. Mark the limit.
Find the first clash. Do the quick sum for each option.
Try the smallest quick sum. Hold that activity back.
No clash left? That is the minimum completion time.
A clash left? Do the quick sums at the new clash, add them to the list, and try the smallest on the whole list.

slides.brief: The routine as a formal card. Each step appears on a click.

slides.title: Try G: no clash left

els.text: G is held until 16, so it runs from 16 to 24.
Minimum completion time: 24 days (1 more than 23).

slides.brief: Level 1 worked example. G is shown held until 16. Pupils write up the answer.

slides.title: Quick sums

items.title: Work out the quick sum
question: Unlimited time is $20$.
An option has LFT $14$ and new finish $16$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: Quick sum is unlimited time plus how late the held activity finishes.

items.title: Work out the quick sum
question: Unlimited time is $25$.
An option has LFT $12$ and new finish $13$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: Quick sum is unlimited time plus how late the held activity finishes.

items.title: Finishes exactly on its LFT
question: Unlimited time is $18$.
An option has LFT $15$ and new finish $15$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: If the held activity still finishes by its LFT, the project time does not change.
explanation: It finishes by its LFT, so the time does not change: $18$.

items.title: Finishes before its LFT
question: Unlimited time is $30$.
An option has LFT $22$ and new finish $20$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: If the held activity still finishes by its LFT, the project time does not change.
explanation: It finishes before its LFT, so the time does not change: $30$.

items.title: Which option first?
answer: A $28$, B $27$, C $26$. Try C first.
question: Unlimited time is $24$.
A: LFT $10$, new finish $14$.
B: LFT $12$, new finish $15$.
C: LFT $9$, new finish $11$.
Find each quick sum. Which option is tried first?
items.rationale: Try the smallest quick sum first.
explanation: The smallest is C, so try C first.

items.title: Which option first?
answer: D $33$, E $31$, F $34$. Try E first: it adds no extra time.
question: Unlimited time is $31$.
D: LFT $17$, new finish $19$.
E: LFT $19$, new finish $19$.
F: LFT $15$, new finish $18$.
Find each quick sum. Which is tried first, and what does it tell you?
items.rationale: Try the smallest quick sum first.
explanation: E is smallest. If its try leaves no clash, the minimum is $31$: no extra time.

items.title: Can it happen?
answer: No. The quick sum is a floor: the project cannot finish before $29$.
question: An option has quick sum $29$.
After trying it, the project finishes at $27$.
Is that possible? Explain.
items.rationale: A try can never finish below its quick sum.
explanation: A quick sum is the earliest the project can possibly finish if that activity is held back.

slides.brief: Seven quick-sum questions climbing from the formula to the floor idea. No pictures: the point is the calculation and why the smallest goes first.

Between 8 and 12, D needs 3 and E needs 4: that is 7 workers, but the limit is 6.

slides.title: Level 2: quick sums

els.text: Unlimited time = 24 days. The clash is 8 to 12, so the options are D and E.

E is held until D finishes at 14, so it runs 14 to 18. D is held until E finishes at 12, so it runs 12 to 20.
The smallest is E (28). Try E first.

slides.brief: Level 2 worked example. Same table, same formula. Pupils fill the last three columns, then show answers. Unlimited time is 24.

slides.title: Level 2: try E

els.text: E runs 14 to 18. F, G and H have to wait for it, so they move later too.
Minimum completion time: 28 days (4 more than 24).

slides.title: Your turn

els.text:
1.  Draw the histogram and the limit line.
2.  Find the first clash. Write the quick sum for each option.
3.  Try the smallest quick sum.
4.  No clash left? Write down the minimum completion time.
5.  Check: it is the smallest quick sum, and it needs no clash.

slides.brief: Pupils practise on the Critical Path tool: Resource levelling, Level 1 then Level 2. Use the routine card on the previous slides.

els.text: When the first try still leaves a clash

slides.title: Level 3: a knock-on clash

els.text: Unlimited time = 21. The first clash is 1 to 6.
Try C (smallest, 22). It leaves a new clash at 14 to 15: F, G and H.

The new quick sums join the same list: F 23, G 22, H 29.
The smallest on the whole list is G (22). Try G: no clash left. Minimum: 22.

slides.brief: Level 3 worked example (10 activities, 2 workers, unlimited 21). Click through the list. Only the numbers are shown, no histograms.

slides.title: Level 3: going back

els.text: Unlimited time = 25. The first clash is 10 to 16.
Try H (smallest, 25). It leaves a new clash. The new quick sums are G 29, H 27, I 27.
The whole list: H 25 (tried), G 26, H 27, I 27, G 29, F 31. The smallest untried is G 26, from the first clash. None of the new options beat it, so go back and try G.
Try G: no clash left. Minimum: 26 (1 more than 25).

slides.brief: Level 3 worked example (11 activities, 2 workers, unlimited 25). Shows the go-back: the new options are all bigger than an untried one from the first list.

els.text: Mei says: "The smallest quick sum is always the minimum completion time." Is she right?
Only if its try leaves no clash. A quick sum is a floor, not always the answer.
In the going-back example, H has the smallest quick sum, 25. Why is the minimum 26, not 25?
Holding H leaves a clash, so 25 is only a floor. The first try with no clash is G, giving 26.

slides.title: In the exam

els.text: Look first. Do any activities need more than half the workers, so they can never run together? Add them up and see.
Use the routine: quick sums, smallest first, until a try leaves no clash.
Stuck? Draw a levelled histogram anyway. A valid schedule scores 2 of the 3 marks even if it is not the best.

slides.brief: Exam technique for questions that do not fit the routine neatly (queues of heavy activities). Per Harry: look first, then the routine, then draw.

items.title: Work out the quick sum
question: Unlimited time is $27$.
An option has LFT $24$ and new finish $31$.
Work out the quick sum.
items.rationale: Quick sum is unlimited time plus how late the held activity finishes.

items.title: Which option first?
question: Three options have quick sums $30$, $28$ and $33$.
Which is tried first?
items.rationale: Try the smallest quick sum first.
explanation: Try the smallest quick sum first: $28$.

items.title: Can it be 30?
answer: No. Every option has a quick sum of at least $31$, so nothing can finish sooner.
question: The smallest quick sum on the list is $31$.
Can the minimum completion time be $30$? Explain.
items.rationale: A quick sum is a floor.
explanation: A quick sum is a floor, so the minimum can never be below $31$.

slides.brief: Last 5 minutes. Question 1 checks the formula, 2 the order, 3 the floor idea.

els.text:
•  A clash is a time when more workers are needed than the limit.
•  Quick sum = unlimited time + (new finish − LFT). It is a floor.
•  Try the smallest quick sum first. No clash left? That is the minimum.
•  Level 3: a try can leave a new clash. Add its quick sums to the same list and take the smallest on the whole list, even if that means going back.
•  Exam: look first, then the routine, then draw it.
